description:
On 2026-10-09, after the unpinned install (#2831), muse was selected three times on canary runs and gave a parseable verdict only once:
- run 37982258535 (PR #2842): "invalid: the verdict must have exactly the keys ('status', 'incomplete_reason', 'decision', 'summary', 'files_examined', 'defects', 'prior_defects')";
- run 37983182017 (PR #2842, next head): valid verdict, SHIP;
- run 37986952599 (PR #2845, oracle-verdict.yml): "invalid: the reviewer output is not JSON: Extra data".
All three ran Muse Code 1.4.4 (1.4.4-R5419.1). An invalid answer counts as absent, so the next reviewer runs and nothing passes wrongly. Impact: the result stays pending only when muse is the only eligible reviewer. That happens when claude is excluded (it is by default, because every PR is treated as claude-authored; see oracle-author-family-labels-never-applied-20261009) and codex is out of quota.

The muse command (_project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/commands.py:74-89) passes no schema flag. The schema reaches muse only as text in the prompt, so wrong keys and extra text are possible.

Investigate. The existing attempt artifacts are only 456 and 408 bytes and expire on 2026-10-16, so they hold no raw output. Obtain raw muse output from a local `muse exec` run with the same brief and schema-in-prompt, or add a new diagnostic capture of the raw (redacted) output for failing runs. Determine whether the extra data is a trailing message, several JSON objects, or prose around the JSON, and whether the wrong keys are a schema drift in the muse model's answer. Compare with `verdict.parse_output` for the muse harness.

Possible fixes, to decide after the evidence: make parse_output take the last complete JSON object from muse's output, strengthen the schema instruction in the muse prompt, or move muse later in the tier orders. Also related: oracle-self-attested-file-list-reviewers-20261008 (muse's file list is self-attested).

Guardrails. An unparseable or wrong-shape answer must never pass; it stays absent. Never weaken the required oracle-review check. Very-high tier; normal oracle PR flow.
